clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old man with morbid obesity, COPD, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes presented with a 1-week history of acute onset rapidly progressive erythematous rash in the deep folds of his pannus and intertriginous areas. Initial clinical impression was candidal intertrigo or erythrasma, and empiric treatment with oral erythromycin and fluconazole was started. Within 3 days of presentation, the rash spread diffusely across the trunk and extremities, forming erythematous morbilliform papules that coalesced into plaques. Within 12 hours of the noticeably worsening rash, the patient acutely decompensated, developing dyspnea, metabolic and respiratory acidosis, requiring ICU transfer and intubation. Erythromycin and fluconazole were immediately discontinued on acute decompensation. Broad-spectrum antibiotics (vancomycin, meropenem, micafungin) were initiated due to concern for septic shock. However, infectious workup was negative (normal CXR, negative CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, negative blood and urine cultures). Skin biopsy was performed and revealed diffuse spongiosis and numerous subcorneal pustules filled with a mixed inflammatory infiltrate predominantly consisting of neutrophils with some associated lymphocytes, establishing the diagnosis of AGEP. Upon AGEP diagnosis, treatment was changed to methylprednisolone 80 mg every 8 hours for 3 days followed by oral steroid taper. The patient had marked improvement in both hemodynamics and rash once started on steroids, was extubated on day 3 of methylprednisolone therapy, required 4 days of continuous venovenous hemodialysis (CVVHD) with complete recovery of kidney and liver function, and was maintained on oral prednisone with slow taper for 2 weeks.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with acute onset rapidly progressive erythematous rash in intertriginous areas over 1 week
Within 3 days, rash spread diffusely across trunk and extremities forming erythematous morbilliform papules coalescing into plaques
Within 12 hours of worsening rash, patient acutely decompensated with dyspnea, metabolic and respiratory acidosis requiring ICU transfer and intubation
Skin biopsy showed diffuse spongiosis and numerous subcorneal pustules filled with mixed inflammatory infiltrate predominantly consisting of neutrophils with some associated lymphocytes
Histopathologic findings are diagnostic of AGEP
Infectious workup was negative including normal CXR, negative CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, negative blood and urine cultures
Erythromycin and fluconazole were immediately discontinued on acute decompensation
Broad-spectrum antibiotics (vancomycin, meropenem, micafungin) were started due to concern for septic shock but were discontinued when infectious workup was negative
Patient was treated with methylprednisolone 80 mg every 8 hours for 3 days with eventual slow taper on oral steroids

Patient had marked improvement in hemodynamics and rash once started on steroids, was extubated on day 3 of methylprednisolone, required 4 days of CVVHD with complete recovery of kidney and liver function, and was maintained on oral prednisone with slow taper for 2 weeks

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Initial clinical suspicion but ruled out by negative fungal cultures and histopathology showing subcorneal pustules with neutrophilic infiltrate rather than candidal elements
Initial clinical suspicion but ruled out by histopathology showing subcorneal pustules with neutrophilic infiltrate and negative infectious workup
Negative CXR, negative CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, negative blood and urine cultures, and polymicrobial skin swab consistent with normal skin flora rather than pathogenic infection

remaining_uncertainties: Specific medication history prior to rash onset and temporal relationship between drug exposure and rash onset (whether erythromycin was started before rash appeared or was empiric treatment after rash was already present)
Whether erythromycin itself triggered AGEP or if another medication was the culprit
